speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your episodes of dizziness and vertigo, could you please tell me if your vertigo is triggered by specific head movements, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since your vertigo is clearly position-dependent, how long does each spinning episode typically last? Additionally, have you noticed any associated symptoms like hearing loss in one ear, ringing in the ears, or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given the classic presentation of position-dependent vertigo without auditory symptoms or neurological deficits, I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver for confirmation. If available, I would also like to see a quick image of your inner ear anatomy to visualize otoconia displacement.
